senses.gloss:
akhaṇḍākāra-vṛtti
(‘modification in the form of the Partless’)
------------------------------------------
Advaita Vedānta advocates nidi-dhyāsana or meditation on the nature of the आत्मन् as the means for its realization. This should be preceded by śravaṇa (hearing about the आत्मन् from the गुरु or preceptor) and मनन (reflection leading to a clear concept and conviction). Once the nature of the आत्मन् is comprehended, and a clear idea formed in the मिन्द्, maturing into a deep conviction, meditation can be proceeded with.
In meditation, the मिन्द् takes the form of the object presented to it. Such modifications are called vṛttis and are like waves unto water. When each succeeding wave is similar to the preceding wave, meditation results.
The object of such meditation in Advaita Vedānta is the आत्मन् itself, which again is identical in its essence with Brah-man, the Absolute. ब्रह्मन् is akhaṇḍa, partless, since it is a homogeneous reality, nay, the only Reality that exists. So, when the मिन्द् starts meditating on ब्रह्मन् which is akhaṇḍa, its vṛttis take on the form of akhaṇḍa-ब्रह्मन्. Such vṛttis are called akhaṇḍākāra-vṛttis. When this meditation ripens into समाधि (absolute concentration), the vṛttis die down and akhaṇḍa-ब्रह्मन् stands revealed.
See also NIDIDHYĀSANA.
